risk_rules.reason: Authentication, MCP grants, and filter enforcement require explicit security and contract review.
Credential/deployment/CI configuration crosses an operational trust boundary.
Dependency and image-install changes affect the software supply chain and deployed runtime compatibility.
Shared state, cursor, replay, and recovery need broader reliability context.

required_checks.reason: Dependency manifests are packaging inputs; base AGENTS requires portal-impact review and portal-contract CI evidence for packaging changes. Bind evidence to the target repository and exact head from the configured GitHub check app; missing or mismatched evidence is UNKNOWN, and a failing check remains FAIL.
Base AGENTS requires portal impact and relevant browser-journey check evidence. This static pilot does not execute target code; evidence absent stays explicit.

rules: Engine adapters classify errors rather than leak exceptions; internal schemas remain independent of wire representations.
MCP search paths share a fail-closed policy gate; sensitive grants are independent and mixed forbidden requests reject atomically.
Report actual filter enforcement; supported parameters alone do not demonstrate enforcement.
Valkey owns shared state; review replay, cursor, cache and snapshot consistency.
Portal is first-class; search, policy, serialization, configuration and engine changes need portal-impact review and applicable checks.
Honor import-linter architecture boundaries; generic code-smell preferences alone are nonblocking.

review_criteria.correctness: Review intended changed behavior against base/head and supplied contracts: failure paths, exception handling, state consistency, concurrency, replay/recovery, API compatibility and callers. Separate observed facts from assumptions. Flag concrete introduced or re-exposed regressions; do not attribute unrelated base defects to this change. Ask for missing critical context as a typed gap.
review_criteria.tests: Assess whether changed tests independently assert behavior, negative and boundary cases, failure/recovery paths and relevant contracts. A mock or test assertion is not execution evidence; never claim tests ran. Cosmetic coverage percentages and tautological tests do not establish behavioral correctness. Missing test suggestions are nonblocking unless concrete material risk or trusted policy makes them required.
review_criteria.maintainability: Honor trusted project conventions and architecture boundaries. Consider cohesive responsibilities, coupling, complexity, clarity and operational failure visibility with concrete consequences. Generic book/style preferences and mechanical smell counts alone do not justify blockers. Keep actionable suggestions proportional to the change.
review_criteria.design: Assess explicit contracts, module responsibilities, abstraction leakage, dependencies and caller compatibility using supplied project context; generic preference alone is not a blocker.
review_criteria.security: Explicitly inspect authentication and authorization, fail-closed policy, mixed request atomicity, source/control/sink paths, input handling, secrets exposure and trust-boundary changes. Substantiate plausible reach and consequence with actual code evidence; static alerts and absent context are not proof. A diff review is not application-wide security certification.
review_criteria.performance: Assess plausible complexity, resource bounds, shared-state races and backpressure with concrete workloads from supplied evidence. Do not invent measured timings, costs or regressions.
review_criteria.project_specific: Apply only trusted project rules and their consequences; report unsupported or missing rule evidence rather than inventing requirements.
